column1: # Clauses of LRM Clause 11 (docs/ch11-vpi.html) that carry no obligation a
# fixture could exercise in either direction: overview prose, the routine
# catalogue, and the diagram legend. Each row quotes the text that makes it so.
# Every other Clause 11 clause is cited by a fixture in this directory
# (p04_*.c for the object model), not classified.

column3: Clause 11 and Clause 12 specify the Verilog Procedural Interface (VPI) for the Verilog-AMS HDL. This clause describes how the VPI routines are used and Clause 12 defines each of the routines in alphabetical order. — a map of the two clauses; the rules are in the subclauses.

The VPI interface provides routines which allow Verilog-AMS product users to access information contained in a Verilog-AMS design ... The functions of the VPI interface can be grouped into two main areas: Dynamic software product interaction using VPI callbacks; Access to Verilog-AMS HDL objects and simulation specific objects — the two areas are 11.2.1 and 11.2.2, each cited on its own.

The VPI routines can be divided into groups based on primary functionality. followed by Tables 11-1 to 11-10, which list routine names under category headings; each routine's behaviour is its Clause 12 subclause.

This clause contains the keys to the symbols used in the object model diagrams. Keys are provided for objects and classes, traversing relationships, and accessing properties. — the keys themselves are 11.5.1-11.5.3.

Bold letters in a solid enclosure indicate an object definition ... Italic letters in a dotted enclosure indicate a class reference ... A dotted enclosure with no name is an unnamed class. — typography of the diagrams, with no routine or result attached (11.5.2 and 11.5.3 carry those, and are cited by p04_01/p04_02).

Subclauses in 11.6.1 through 11.6.25 contain the data model diagrams that define the accessible objects and groups of objects, along with their relationships and properties. — an index of its subclauses, each cited by the p04 applications.
